test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 8 June 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Sawdust is used to adulterate:
solution:
The correct answer is **coriander powder**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chemicals that become contaminants **when mixed with other chemicals are** known as adulterants**. To increase the quantity while lowering the quality, adulterants are introduced to** pure substances.**
 
• This spice is contaminated with husk, ash, and dung powder.** Consuming tainted coriander powder** might result in gas, constipation, and **cramping in the stomach.**
 
• **In general, food is considered **adulterated if it contains a dangerous or harmful chemical that could endanger human health. Examples of tainted foods include Brie cheese contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes and **apple cider contaminated with E. coli O157:H7. **
 
• **Coriander powder is also adulterated with sawdust.** The procedure used to check for adulterants in the case of the chilli powder can be utilised. **Tea granules sawdust** can be used to tamper with loose tea powder. Adulterators mix artificial colour along with** some flavours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acetic acid and water are combined to create vinegar **through a two-step fermentation process. First, yeast consume any liquid derived from a plant source, such as fruits, whole grains, potatoes, or rice, and feed on the sugar or starch therein. It ferments** into alcohol.**
 
• **Cheese is a dairy product** made from the coagulation of milk protein casein. It comes in a broad variety of flavours, textures, and forms. It is made out of milk-derived proteins and fat, typically from the **milk of cows, buffalo, goats, or sheep.**
 
• In essence, **milk is an emulsion of fat, protein, dissolved sugar (carbohydrate),** minerals, and vitamins in water. All mammals' milk contains these ingredients, though the amounts vary between and within **species and across species. **
